# Te Pāti Māori Vow To Protect Te Tiriti With Establishment Of Independent Commissioner For Te Tiriti O Waitangi

*Tuesday, 4 February 2025, 4:32 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2502/S00022/te-pati-maori-vow-to-protect-te-tiriti-with-esta.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2502/S00022/te-pati-maori-vow-to-protect-te-tiriti-with-esta.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori today announced a bold commitment to protect and uphold the mana of Te Tiriti o Waitangi by establishing a Parliamentary Commissioner for Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

Co-leaders Debbie Ngarewa-Packer and Rawiri Waititi made the announcement at the Waitangi Treaty Grounds. Te Pāti Māori says this is a critical step to ensure the Crown is held accountable for its obligations under Aotearoa’s founding document.

“Our people have waited far too long for the promises of Te Tiriti to be honoured. This Commissioner will be an independent advocate, ensuring that Te Tiriti is honoured across all government policies and decisions made in Parliament,” said Ngarewa-Packer.

“The commissioner would have the role of auditing the government in being honourable of Te Tiriti o Waitangi. It will provide independent advice to Parliament, and ensure Māori voices are central to decision-making processes.

“We must continue to build the Aotearoa hou that tangata whenua and tangata tiriti are envisioning. That must start with committing to the promise of Te Tiriti o Waitangi."

The announcement comes as Aotearoa prepares to commemorate Waitangi Day, following the Te Pāti Māori caucus wānanga in Paihia.

“We have heard the harmonious call from Aotearoa to make this a one-term government,” said Rawiri Waititi.

“Our discussions in caucus this week have focused on coalition negotiations and how we must centralise Te Tiriti in all policy. This starts with an independent Parliamentary Commissioner.

“Crown-led approaches have consistently failed to uphold the commitments promised in Te Tiriti.

“We see the importance of an independent Parliamentary Commissioner. It’s time for a dedicated watchdog to protect the rights of tangata whenua and ensure government actions align with tino rangatiratanga, equity, and active protection.”

Te Pāti Māori calls on all political parties to support this crucial initiative and stand on the right side of history by giving mana to Te Tiriti.

documents/2026-01-28-if-youre-not-trying.text:
# “If You’re Not Trying To Abolish Prisons In Aotearoa, What Are You Doing In Parliament?” - Rawiri Waititi

*Wednesday, 28 January 2026, 12:50 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2601/S00112/if-youre-not-trying-to-abolish-prisons-in-aotearoa-what-are-you-doing-in-parliament-rawiri-waititi.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2601/S00112/if-youre-not-trying-to-abolish-prisons-in-aotearoa-what-are-you-doing-in-parliament-rawiri-waititi.htm)

## Full text

Political parties from across the House have used our longstanding policy to abolish prisons as an opportunity to scare the public, despite decades of evidence proving that prisons don’t work. Te Pāti Māori stands firmly behind our policy of creating an Aotearoa where prisons are not needed.

“Decades of evidence from Aotearoa and across the globe has made it absolutely clear that prisons are completely ineffective at deterring crime, rehabilitating offenders, and lowering re-offending rates” said Te Pāti Māori Co-leader and Justice Spokesperson, Rawiri Waititi.

“Over half of all prisoners reoffend within two years of their release because these institutions were never designed for rehabilitation.

“Prisons don’t work because they do nothing to address the root causes of crime: poverty, inequality, unemployment, homelessness, racism, poor mental health, and trauma.

“We want to move resources away from ineffective prisons towards effective prevention, rehabilitation, and community-led solutions.

“Our entire policy platform is designed to eliminate the root causes of crime; we want to create an Aotearoa where prisons are redundant.

“This isn’t going to happen overnight, but there are immediate steps we can take to achieving this goal: We can repeal three strikes, we can decriminalise drug use, we can make sure every person is housed, and we can reform the tax and social security system to curb inequality, and lift people out of poverty.

“Countries like Norway are already well on their way to eliminating prisons. Instead of large, centralised prisons, Norway has a system of small, community-based correctional facilities that focus on rehabilitation and reintegration into society.

“We are not going to abolish prisons when we are in government in 2026, but we are going to start building an Aotearoa where this becomes a possibility.

“We need a transformative move; focussed on rehabilitation, reintegration and recidivism rather than punishment and incarceration. Our movement is about being hard on healing rather than hard on crime!” Waititi said.

# Oriini Kaipara: Prime Minister’s ‘Progress’ Ignores Housing Crisis Facing Māori And Rangatahi

*Thursday, 29 January 2026, 8:52 am Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2601/S00115/oriini-kaipara-prime-ministers-progress-ignores-housing-crisis-facing-maori-and-rangatahi.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2601/S00115/oriini-kaipara-prime-ministers-progress-ignores-housing-crisis-facing-maori-and-rangatahi.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori MP for Tāmaki Makaurau, Oriini Kaipara, has delivered a strong reply to the Prime Minister’s Statement in Parliament, saying the Government’s claims of “progress and prosperity” are disconnected from the lived reality of Māori and thousands of whānau facing homelessness and housing insecurity.

“The Prime Minister painted a picture of a stronger Aotearoa. For Māori, especially in Tāmaki Makaurau, that picture is fiction. Mum would say it’s all kaka,” Ms Kaipara said.

Ms Kaipara criticised what she described as two years of anti-Māori and anti-Tiriti policies that have stripped away rights, undermined te reo and tikanga Māori, and worsened the housing crisis.

“What’s despicable is that this Government is comfortable pushing whānau Māori deeper into crisis. Nowhere is that crisis more visible or more brutal than in housing,” she said.

The Prime Minister claimed the Government is making “good progress” on housing. Ms Kaipara rejected that assertion.

“Giving $3 billion in tax cuts to landlords is not progress. Making it harder to access emergency housing is not progress. Selling homes to overseas buyers for holiday houses is not progress. The only progress these policies make is toward homelessness.”

Ms Kaipara said the housing crisis represents one of the greatest modern breaches of Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

“The greatest breach of Te Tiriti is when tangata whenua have no whenua and no home.”

She highlighted alarming homelessness statistics, noting that more than 110,000 people in Aotearoa are currently without stable housing.

“More than half of them are rangatahi - our future leaders - sleeping on the streets. A third are wāhine Māori, many of them pregnant or new mothers. Service providers are overwhelmed, and kaupapa Māori services like Te Whare Hinatore at Auckland City Mission are being forced to turn whānau away.”

Ms Kaipara said the crisis could be ended immediately with political courage.

“There are 112,000 empty houses across this country - ghost houses, Whare Kēhua. Why not house our people first? That is not throwing away money. That is securing our future.”

She pointed to her recently introduced Members’ Bill to end youth homelessness as a practical solution.

“My bill focuses on the cure, not the crisis. It is rangatahi-led, evidence-based, and transformational. That is what real progress looks like.”

Ms Kaipara said real leadership would require embedding Te Tiriti o Waitangi across all laws, prioritising people over profit, and protecting Papatūānuku.

“That is the time Prime Ministers should celebrate. But that time is not today.”

Speaking on behalf of Tāmaki Makaurau and as Te Pāti Māori’s housing spokesperson, Ms Kaipara issued a clear message to the Government:

“We will not accept any more broken promises.

We will not accept the erosion of our rights.

We will not accept a future where Māori and the people of Aotearoa are left behind in our own whenua.”

“Our people deserve better.

Tāmaki Makaurau deserves better.

Aotearoa deserves better.”

Alongside Kaipara’s Members’ bill, Te Pāti Māori’s housing policy includes:

- Building 2000 houses on papakāinga

- Radically increasing public housing investment

- Allocating 50% of new social housing builds to whānau Māori who make up 50% of the social housing waitlist

- Stopping all sales of freehold land to offshore foreign interests

- Taxing Property Investors

- Supporting renters through universal rent control, and repealing no cause evictions

# Seabed Mining Banned In Aotearoa Under Reintroduced Member’s Bill

*Sunday, 8 February 2026, 3:25 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2602/S00040/seabed-mining-banned-in-aotearoa-under-reintroduced-members-bill.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2602/S00040/seabed-mining-banned-in-aotearoa-under-reintroduced-members-bill.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori Co-Leader Debbie Ngarewa-Packer has reintroduced her second Member’s Bill to permanently ban seabed mining in Aotearoa, fast-track or not.

“The evidence is now undeniable,” said Ngarewa-Packer.

“Even under fast-track legislation designed to push projects through, seabed mining has been found to cause unacceptable harm to the environment, to taonga species, and to tikanga Māori.”

Ngarewa-Packer said opposition to seabed mining was a defining reason she entered Parliament.

“Protecting our moana and standing with coastal iwi and hapū is why I got into politics in the first place. This Bill is about finishing what we started and making sure these protections are finally locked in for future generations.”

The Seabed Mining Prohibition Act closes all legal pathways for seabed mining, including fast-track approvals, and applies across the coastal marine area, the exclusive economic zone, and the continental shelf.

“This Bill reflects what iwi, hapū, scientists, and coastal communities have been saying for years these impacts cannot be conditioned away.”

Ngarewa-Packer said the Bill builds on her previous seabed mining legislation, received the support of the Green Party was voted down by Labour.

“This version has been strengthened to reflect changes to the law, including fast-track legislation.”

“When regulators themselves conclude that the risks are too great and the uncertainty too high, Parliament has a responsibility to act.”

“This is about mana moana, kaitiakitanga, and intergenerational responsibility. Our oceans are not sacrifice zones and this is work I intend to see through.”

The Bill has been prepared for lodging in the Members’ Bill ballot this week.

# Māori Seats Are Constitutional, Not Conditional

*Friday, 13 February 2026, 1:52 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2602/S00082/maori-seats-are-constitutional-not-conditional.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2602/S00082/maori-seats-are-constitutional-not-conditional.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori co-leader Rawiri Waititi says New Zealand First’s proposed referendum on the Māori seats is a constitutional attack driven by fear of Māori political power.

“Māori representation in Parliament is not conditional on whether Winston Peters approves of how Māori MPs behave,” said Waititi.

“The era of being told to be good Māori is over. The Māori seats exist because of our constitutional history and the systematic exclusion of Māori from power. They are not a privilege that can be revoked when someone is uncomfortable with our strength.”

“The Māori electorates were created in 1867 to keep Māori out of Parliament, not give us representation,” Waititi said.

“Māori far outnumbered Pākehā when Parliament was established. If we’d had equal voting rights, every MP, including the Prime Minister, would have been Māori. The four seats were designed to cap our power at a level that kept us politically powerless.”

“We have reclaimed them and made them instruments of rangatiratanga. They are guaranteed under Te Tiriti o Waitangi.”

Te Pāti Māori is challenging the Prime Minister to immediately rule out the referendum.

“If Chris Luxon has any credibility, he would immediately rule out a referendum on the constitutional status of Māori representation,” said Waititi.

“The Māori electorates belong to te iwi Māori. They cannot be voted away by those who fear our political strength.”

“Every major poll shows Te Pāti Māori will be kingmaker this election,” Waititi concluded.

“When we form the next government, we will entrench the Māori seats in the constitution beyond the reach of referendums driven by fear and colonial reflex.”

# Te Pāti Māori Rejects Move-on Orders: “We Will Not Police Our Way Out Of Homelessness"

*Sunday, 22 February 2026, 8:30 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2602/S00141/te-pati-maori-rejects-move-on-orders-we-will-not-police-our-way-out-of-homelessness.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2602/S00141/te-pati-maori-rejects-move-on-orders-we-will-not-police-our-way-out-of-homelessness.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori has denounced the Government’s plan to increase police powers to issue ‘move-on’ orders banning homeless people from public spaces, across Aotearoa.

Housing and Homelessness spokesperson Oriini Kaipara warns the move will deepen harm for the most vulnerable, while allowing the system to continue profiting from their exclusion.

“It is not about public safety or protecting people. It is about protecting businesses,” Kaipara said.

“It targets those who have the absolute least. It does nothing to end homelessness. It does nothing to house our most vulnerable. It is a poor attempt at fixing a pakaru pipeline that puts people in poverty in prison."

Earlier today, the government announced its intentions to amend the Summary Offences Act that allows police to issue ‘move-on’ orders banning beggars, rough sleepers, and anyone displaying disorderly or threatening behaviour from public spaces, for up to 24 hours.

The new rule would apply to anyone aged 14 years and over, if breached, a person could be fined up to $2,000 or jailed for up to three months.

“Criminalising poverty is a serious constitutional move, one that steers us farther from our proud culture of manaaki, as people of Aotearoa,” Kaipara says.

“When we punish our own instead of supporting them to get better and back on their feet, we are ultimately abandoning our responsibility of care to one another.

Despite several government solutions including Housing First and Transitional Housing providing relief across centres, housing demand remains at crisis point, nationwide.

There are around 110,000 people homeless in Aotearoa, almost half are under 25. In Tāmaki Makaurau, the figure doubled to 940.

The MP for Tāmaki Makaurau warns the ‘move-on’ orders directly conflict with the urgent need to reduce homelessness and build pathways into stability and intergenerational security.

“We will not police our way out of homelessness,” Kaipara said.

“Māori remain significantly overrepresented in homelessness and incarceration statistics. Instead of investing in housing, the government is choosing enforcement. That will push whānau further into cycles of instability, insecurity, and ultimately crime.

Kaipara is calling for immediate action aligned with Māori-led solutions and prevention.

“Our people are not the problem. The failure to provide housing is.”

“Rangatahi are most at risk. Advocacy groups including Manaaki Rangatahi have urged the government and Ministers for years to end the homeless crisis by investing in youth-centred, Māori solutions.

“This is exactly what my first Member’s Bill, the Youth Homelessness Prevention Bill, seeks to achieve. It is by the people, for the people.”

### MP Tāmaki Makaurau Housing Priorities (include):

- Large-scale investment in Māori-led housing developments

- Immediate implementation of rangatahi homelessness prevention pathways

- Direct funding to iwi and Māori housing providers

- Expansion of Housing First and wrap-around services

- Long-term strategies that enable Māori housing independence and development

documents/2026-03-01-te-pati-maori-state.text:
# Te Pāti Māori Statement: Aotearoa Must Stand For Peace

*Sunday, 1 March 2026, 5:19 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2603/S00004/te-pati-maori-statement-aotearoa-must-stand-for-peace.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2603/S00004/te-pati-maori-statement-aotearoa-must-stand-for-peace.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori stands firmly opposed to war and military escalation in Iran and across the Middle East.

We reject the idea that bombing, invasion, or unilateral military strikes create peace. History shows us the opposite. Military aggression destabilises regions, costs civilian lives, and deepens generational trauma.

Two truths can exist at once. Authoritarian regimes can be oppressive. And foreign military intervention driven by geopolitical interests does not liberate ordinary people. It is everyday families who pay the price. Bombing innocent girls at their school is monstrous!

As Indigenous people, we know what it means when powerful nations justify force in the name of “security”, “order”, or “freedom”. Too often those words mask economic interests, strategic dominance, and political ego. The legacy is displacement, grief, and long-term instability.

Aotearoa must not be silent or complicit. Our foreign policy should be grounded in international law, multilateral diplomacy, and the protection of civilian life. We call on the New Zealand Government to:

• Publicly condemn unilateral military aggression

• Advocate for immediate de-escalation

• Support diplomatic pathways through the United Nations

• Prioritise humanitarian aid and civilian protection

Peace is not naïve. Diplomacy is not weakness. International law is not optional.

War has never delivered enduring safety for ordinary people. It delivers profit for arms dealers and political theatre for leaders, while families bury their loved ones.

Te Pāti Māori stands for peace, sovereignty, and the protection of human life everywhere.

Kia tau te rangimārie.

# Te Pāti Māori Calls For Urgent Suspension Of Fuel Excise Tax To Relieve Pressure On Whānau

*Wednesday, 18 March 2026, 10:29 am Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2603/S00110/te-pati-maori-calls-for-urgent-suspension-of-fuel-excise-tax-to-relieve-pressure-on-whanau.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2603/S00110/te-pati-maori-calls-for-urgent-suspension-of-fuel-excise-tax-to-relieve-pressure-on-whanau.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori is calling on the Government to immediately suspend fuel excise tax to provide urgent relief for whānau already feeling the strain at the petrol pump.

“We cannot afford to sit back and wait for a full-blown crisis before we act. Our people are already hurting” said Te Pāti Māori Co-leader and Finance spokesperson Rawiri Waititi.

“For the wealthy, rising fuel prices is an inconvenience, for everyone else it’s a lifeline. For whānau in rural, isolated, and low-income areas without viable public transport options, higher petrol prices mean harder access to work, harder access to healthcare, higher food costs and increased financial stress across the board” Waititi said.

Te Pāti Māori says the Government must act now to take immediate pressure off household budgets by removing the excise component of fuel pricing.

“For an average whānau filling a 50-litre tank, fuel excise adds around $35 every time they fill up. Suspending fuel excise is the fastest way to put money back into people’s pockets immediately."

“The government has failed to invest in affordable and accessible public transport. Until the happens, our whānau will continue depend on fossil fuels for survival.”

“Global instability will continue to drive up fuel costs. The question is whether this Government is willing to act before the pressure becomes unbearable.”

“We’ve seen this before. During COVID, Māori communities and organisations led from the front. We moved early, we protected our people, and we got results" Waititi said.

documents/2026-04-02-te-pati-maori-calls.title: Te Pāti Māori Calls For Freeze On MP Pay Rises
documents/2026-04-02-te-pati-maori-calls.text:
# Te Pāti Māori Calls For Freeze On MP Pay Rises

*Thursday, 2 April 2026, 11:46 am Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2604/S00015/te-pati-maori-calls-for-freeze-on-mp-pay-rises.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2604/S00015/te-pati-maori-calls-for-freeze-on-mp-pay-rises.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori is calling for an immediate freeze on all salary increases for MPs, Ministers, and the Prime Minister, as politicians prepare to receive a pay bump later this year.

“At a time when whānau are being stretched to breaking point just to put kai on the table, politicians should not be giving themselves a raise, “ said Rawiri Waititi, Te Pāti Māori Co-leader and Finance spokesperson

“It’s daylight robbery.”

Te Pāti Māori says accepting pay rises during one of the toughest economic periods in recent memory is out of touch with the reality facing everyday families.

“We cannot sit here and take more money while our people are struggling to survive. It goes against everything we stand for. It is morally wrong. It is ethically wrong. And it makes no sense economically either.”

The party says the focus should instead be on addressing growing inequality across Aotearoa.

“The government is cashing in on the extra tax revenue from rising fuel and kai costs but has no intention of redistributing it to where it’s needed most.”

“The last thing this country needs is politicians lining their own pockets while whānau go without.”

In May 2025, the Government used urgency to wipe 33 pay equity claims. A year later, after telling women workers there is no money for fairness, politicians are lining up for a pay rise. That is not leadership. It is a disgrace.

Te Pāti Māori is calling for an immediate freeze on MP pay rises and for Ministers and the Prime Minister to take a deeper cut in solidarity with the people they are meant to serve.

We will back pay equity claims, not political privilege.

The money should go to workers, wāhine and whānau, not to politicians who are protected from the worst of this economy.

documents/2026-04-09-must-fund-marae-res.title: Must Fund Marae Resilience Package Ahead Of Cyclone Vaianu
documents/2026-04-09-must-fund-marae-res.text:
# Must Fund Marae Resilience Package Ahead Of Cyclone Vaianu

*Thursday, 9 April 2026, 2:02 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2604/S00046/must-fund-marae-resilience-package-ahead-of-cyclone-vaianu.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2604/S00046/must-fund-marae-resilience-package-ahead-of-cyclone-vaianu.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori is calling on the Government to urgently deliver a dedicated Marae Resilience Package, ensuring marae and communities are fully resourced and prepared ahead of Cyclone Vaianu. Co-leader and Waiariki MP Rawiri Waititi says it is the Government’s responsibility to act before disaster strikes, not after.

“Our first concern is the safety of our people. Marae are often the first-place people turn to in a civil emergency. They need essential access to power, water, supplies, and communications before disaster hits. Marae must be empowered and properly resourced to meet the urgent needs of our communities" said Waititi.

“During emergencies like Cyclone Gabrielle, Covid-19 and the Christchurch earthquakes, marae acted as frontline shelters and coordination hubs without formal support, funding, or legal recognition. Marae cannot continue to carry the magnitude of response needed in the wake of civil emergencies alone.”

Te Pāti Māori is demanding immediate rollout of the Marae Resilience Package, including:

- Formal Recognition of Marae as emergency response hubs

Upfront Government funding for emergency supplies and infrastructure

- Access to generators, water storage, and communications systems

- Long-term investment to strengthen marae as civil defence hubs

Waititi said the potential impact of Cyclone Vaianu highlights the urgent need for proactive Government action.

“These are no longer once in a generation weather events. Year after year our communities carry the load. Many marae are still expected to respond and rebuild without the Government providing any proper support or investment.”

“Marae must be recognised for what they already are, essential. They must be valued as such, and it is the responsibility of the Government to invest in their protection, their sustainability, and their evolution. When our marae thrive, so too do our people.”

Te Pāti Māori urges the Government to act now, and whānau to stay connected, follow local guidance, and check in on kaumātua and neighbours as Cyclone Vaianu approaches

documents/2026-04-09-we-must-act-now-on-.title: We Must Act Now On Energy Sovereignty- Every Household Is Paying The Price
documents/2026-04-09-we-must-act-now-on-.text:
# We Must Act Now On Energy Sovereignty- Every Household Is Paying The Price

*Thursday, 9 April 2026, 9:39 am Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2604/S00042/we-must-act-now-on-energy-sovereignty-every-household-is-paying-the-price.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2604/S00042/we-must-act-now-on-energy-sovereignty-every-household-is-paying-the-price.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori is calling on the Government to urgently invest in Aotearoa’s energy infrastructure and is urging all parties to commit to a cross-party plan to ease the rising cost burden on households, rural communities, marae, and small businesses.

Co-Leader Debbie Ngarewa-Packer says the current crisis has exposed how dangerously vulnerable Aotearoa is to forces beyond our control.

“Until we break our dependency on imported fossil fuels, Aotearoa will always be exposed to global wars and price shocks at the pump, at the supermarket, and in the cost of living. This is not a left or right issue, this is an Aotearoa issue.”

“We are sending around $55 million offshore every day to pay for fossil fuels. Fuel tax relief is temporary. The only way to provide permanent, urgent relief is to invest in our energy infrastructure now.”

Ngarewa-Packer says a government-backed transition is both affordable and achievable, and that the blueprint is straightforward.

“Start with a government-backed rollout to electrify our homes and communities. Deliver mass rooftop solar and battery subsidies. Pay people fairly for the power they generate. Support local and regional community microgrids in rural areas and on marae. Target the biggest energy users and align energy, transport, and housing, including EV uptake, in one national strategy.”

“If we generate our own power, back solar, batteries, and local systems at scale, we can reduce household costs, retain billions of dollars here at home, and build our own energy and economic sovereignty.”

Te Pāti Māori is calling on the Government to work across the House to deliver this transition as a matter of urgency.

“Ceasefires are fragile. Resource wars are a permanent feature of a fossil-fuelled world. We need to get out of that game, and every party in Parliament should be willing to say so.”

documents/2026-05-15-tpm-to-entrench-te-.title: TPM To Entrench Te Tiriti: Government’s Tiriti Purge Is Constitutional Vandalism
documents/2026-05-15-tpm-to-entrench-te-.text:
# TPM To Entrench Te Tiriti: Government’s Tiriti Purge Is Constitutional Vandalism

*Friday, 15 May 2026, 4:29 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2605/S00134/tpm-to-entrench-te-tiriti-governments-tiriti-purge-is-constitutional-vandalism.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2605/S00134/tpm-to-entrench-te-tiriti-governments-tiriti-purge-is-constitutional-vandalism.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori is condemning today’s announcement by Justice Minister Paul Goldsmith to strip or weaken Te Tiriti o Waitangi references across 19 pieces of legislation.

“This is not policy reform. It is constitutional vandalism.”

After failing to redefine Te Tiriti through the Treaty Principles Bill, the Government is now dismantling it clause by clause through legislative review instead. Different vehicle. Same destination.

Among the most aggressive changes are the repeal of Te Tiriti provisions in health, climate, mental health and education legislation, areas where Māori already face entrenched inequity.

Reducing Te Tiriti obligations to merely “take into account” fundamentally undermines partnership and allows the Crown to tick the box and carry on regardless.

They may hold power in this term of Parliament, but they do not hold the authority to erase Te Tiriti.

Every step this Government takes strips away more of the constitutional grounding that protects our people and our taiao.

When this Government moves to erase Te Tiriti, Te Pāti Māori will be there to entrench it.

# If The Government Really Wants To Lower Power Bills, This Is The Way

*Tuesday, 9 June 2026, 8:23 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2606/S00066/if-the-government-really-wants-to-lower-power-bills-this-is-the-way.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2606/S00066/if-the-government-really-wants-to-lower-power-bills-this-is-the-way.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori Co-Leader Debbie Ngarewa-Packer says the government’s LNG announcement today exposes a fundamental failure of energy policy leadership.

“Simeon Brown says he has an answer to our energy security problem. A billion-dollar contract to import liquefied natural gas. From the Middle East. With no plan to pay for it. That’s not energy security, that’s energy dependency,” says Ngarewa-Packer.

“Initially the government planned a levy on power bills to fund this facility. Now they want the same gentailers, companies they’ve spent three years refusing to regulate, to voluntarily fund something those same companies say they don’t need. Meridian said it publicly. They don’t need this terminal.

“So the government is going to sign us up to international gas prices we cannot control, on infrastructure we don’t own, to solve a problem the industry says doesn’t exist. And they’ll work out who pays later.

“New Zealand already generates over 80% of its electricity from renewables. We sit on some of the best geothermal resource in the world. We have rivers, wind, sun. We have iwi and communities ready to build and own local generation right now.

“The dry year problem is real. But the answer is not to plant a gas terminal on our coastline and pray the Strait of Hormuz stays open.

“Invest in storage and demand flexibility so we’re not at the mercy of hydro levels. Expand geothermal, we’ve barely scratched the surface. Put real money behind rooftop solar with feed-in tariffs that actually work. Build community microgrids so rural and Māori communities stop being the last served and first cut off. Use the leverage we already have, the gentailers are state-owned, direct them to treat dry year risk as a public obligation, not a profit line.

“Energy that belongs here. Generation we control. Prices we’re not hostage to. And when the next dry year hits, it won’t be our communities paying the price again.

“That’s energy sovereignty. That’s the only credible solution and Te Pāti Māori will invest in it.”

documents/2026-08-02-te-pati-maori-annou.text:
# Te Pāti Māori Announces Māori Education Authority To Restore Māori Success In Education

*Sunday, 2 August 2026, 2:23 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2608/S00006/te-pati-maori-announces-maori-education-authority-to-restore-maori-success-in-education.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2608/S00006/te-pati-maori-announces-maori-education-authority-to-restore-maori-success-in-education.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori today unveiled its commitment to establish a Māori Education Authority, with Te Tai Tonga candidate Lisa Marie Murch announcing the policy during her debut election debate on Marae.

The policy commits to restoring Māori authority over Māori education by strengthening Māori governance across the education system, investing in kōhanga reo, kura kaupapa Māori, wharekura and wānanga, embedding mātauranga Māori throughout the curriculum, and ensuring every tamaiti has the opportunity to succeed as who they are.

Lisa Marie Murch said the policy is about giving every Māori child the opportunity to thrive.

"Enhancing educational success is my bottom line because every mokopuna deserves the opportunity to succeed as who they are."

"Te Pāti Māori will establish a Māori Education Authority. We will strengthen education for tamariki across all education sectors, support our teachers, and ensure our tamariki grow up proud in their identity, language and culture. Education isn't just about the classroom, it's about the future of our people and ensuring success for generations to come."

Te Pāti Māori Co-Leader Rawiri Waititi said the current education system continues to reflect the legacy of assimilation rather than Māori aspiration.

"For generations our tamariki have been expected to succeed in a system that was never designed for them. A Māori Education Authority puts decision making back where it belongs, with Māori. When our tamariki are grounded in their identity, language and culture, they do not just participate in education, they excel."

Te Pāti Māori Co-Leader Debbie Ngarewa-Packer said Māori leadership in education is essential to achieving equitable outcomes.

"Education is one of the greatest expressions of tino rangatiratanga. Our tamariki deserve an education system that celebrates who they are, values mātauranga Māori, supports our kaiako and walks alongside whānau. This policy invests in generations of Māori success, not just the next school term."

Te Pāti Māori's education policy is founded on the principle that Māori learners thrive when Māori lead, whānau are central to educational success, and education must uphold identity while reflecting Aotearoa's diverse knowledge systems.

The Māori Education Authority forms the cornerstone of Te Pāti Māori's wider education policy, which also includes expanding school lunches, free public transport for all students, free school counselling, making te reo Māori a core curriculum subject through Year 10, increasing student support, and strengthening the education workforce.

# Te Pati Maori Will Make The Waitangi Tribunal Recommendations Binding

*Thursday, 6 August 2026, 9:31 am Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2608/S00044/te-pati-maori-will-make-the-waitangi-tribunal-recommendations-binding.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2608/S00044/te-pati-maori-will-make-the-waitangi-tribunal-recommendations-binding.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori Co-Leader Rawiri Waititi says New Zealand First's call to review the Waitangi Tribunal proves the coalition has learnt nothing from the Tribunal's latest report.

"The Waitangi Tribunal has found that the Government's Treaty clause review is a major breach of Te Tiriti. Instead of fixing the breach, Shane Jones wants to investigate the institution that exposed it."

Waititi says this is about far more than constitutional law.

"It is about accountability. When an independent watchdog tells the Government it has breached Te Tiriti, the Government's job is to address the breach, not attack the watchdog."

Te Pāti Māori says the latest developments expose a deeper flaw in Aotearoa's constitutional arrangements.

"The Waitangi Tribunal can investigate, hear evidence and make findings. But governments can simply ignore them."

"That is why Te Pāti Māori will make Waitangi Tribunal recommendations binding, establish a Parliamentary Commissioner for Te Tiriti, and require every Bill before Parliament to include a Te Tiriti Impact Statement."

Waititi says New Zealanders should ask a simple question.

"If governments can ignore the Waitangi Tribunal every time they don't like the answer, what accountability is left?"

"Our answer is simple. We will ensure that we put mechanisms in place to strengthen the institutions that uphold Te Tiriti instead of allowing others to weaken them."

# Pūtea Back In Your Pocket: TPM Unveils A Kiwi Tax Plan For Everyone

*Wednesday, 26 August 2026, 3:38 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2608/S00238/putea-back-in-your-pocket-tpm-unveils-a-kiwi-tax-plan-for-everyone.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2608/S00238/putea-back-in-your-pocket-tpm-unveils-a-kiwi-tax-plan-for-everyone.htm)

Attachments linked in the release: [https://img.scoop.co.nz/media/pdfs/2608/A_Kiwi_Tax_Plan.pdf](https://img.scoop.co.nz/media/pdfs/2608/A_Kiwi_Tax_Plan.pdf)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori has unveiled an economic plan for the many, not the few, putting more pūtea into the pockets of almost everyone in Aotearoa.

Under the plan, 4.5 million people (97%) will pay less income tax, with the first $30,000 earned tax-free.

Around 4.2 million people (90%) will receive, on average, an additional $4,000 a year.

“This is a policy for everyone. Whether you are a cleaner, a nurse, a teacher, a tradie, a pensioner or raising a whānau, we want you to keep more of what you earn.

“People across Aotearoa are feeling the squeeze. The kai bill is up. Housing costs are up. Power is up. Everything is taking a bigger bite out of the household budget.

“Our answer is simple: put pūtea back in people’s pockets and give Aotearoa some room to breathe.”

The plan also delivers targeted support with kai costs for 3 million people (64%), providing people earning $60,000 or less with a tax credit worth up to eight weeks of kai each year.

The other side of the equation is fairness.

The targeted wealth tax will affect only the wealthiest 3% of people, while 97% will pay no wealth tax at all. The wider plan also asks corporations, offshore profit transfers, vacant property and land banking to contribute more.

“This isn't about Māori versus non-Māori, or workers versus business. It's about building an economy that works for the overwhelming majority of people who call Aotearoa home.

“4.5 million people (97%) pay less income tax. The wealthiest 3% contribute more. That's what a fair economy looks like.”

We have named this the Kiwi Tax Plan because it is a tax policy for everyone, ensuring everyone in Aotearoa has an opportunity to thrive.

# Te Pāti Māori Launches Te Tiriti Entrenchment Policy

*Tuesday, 1 September 2026, 12:47 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2609/S00008/te-pati-maori-launches-te-tiriti-entrenchment-policy.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2609/S00008/te-pati-maori-launches-te-tiriti-entrenchment-policy.htm)

Attachments linked in the release: [https://img.scoop.co.nz/media/pdfs/2609/TIRITI_ENTRENCHMENT_POLICY.pdf](https://img.scoop.co.nz/media/pdfs/2609/TIRITI_ENTRENCHMENT_POLICY.pdf)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori has today launched its Te Tiriti Entrenchment Policy, a major constitutional reform package that will make Crown obligations arising from Te Tiriti legally enforceable and resource the next stage of Māori-led constitutional transformation.

“Te Tiriti is the constitutional foundation of Aotearoa. Its mana does not rise and fall depending on who forms the Government,” Te Pāti Māori Co-Leader Rawiri Waititi said.

“Our policy is about certainty, accountability and making sure the Crown keeps its promises.”

### The policy will:

- establish a $220 million Mātike Mai Fund over four years to independently resource Māori-led constitutional transformation;

- establish an independent Te Tiriti Commission with powers to investigate serious Crown breaches, require remedial action and issue Te Tiriti Compliance Orders;

- make Waitangi Tribunal recommendations binding on the Crown;

- restore and resource a national action plan to implement the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples within the first 100 days; and

- set 2040 as the target for constitutional transformation in Aotearoa.

Mātike Mai is an independent Māori-led constitutional kaupapa. Te Pāti Māori will not determine the constitutional destination. Its role is to resource iwi, hapū and Māori to lead that conversation, and to create the space for tangata Tiriti, local government and the Crown to participate in the national dialogue that follows.

“Under this Government we have seen Te Tiriti protections stripped from legislation and hard-won progress wound back. That has made this work more important than ever,” Te Pāti Māori Co-Leader Debbie Ngarewa-Packer said.

“But this is bigger than one Government.

“A confident and mature Aotearoa should be able to honour its history, keep its promises and build its future together.

“Te Tiriti is not a threat to unity. Honouring Te Tiriti strengthens accountability, creates certainty and gives us a stronger foundation for the country we are building together.

“This legislation binds the Crown, not Te Tiriti.”

# We Want Cheaper Power And We Want Our People To Own It

*Wednesday, 16 September 2026, 12:11 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2609/S00161/we-want-cheaper-power-and-we-want-our-people-to-own-it.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2609/S00161/we-want-cheaper-power-and-we-want-our-people-to-own-it.htm)

Attachments linked in the release: [https://img.scoop.co.nz/media/pdfs/2609/Te_Pti_Mori_Energy_Sovereignty_Policy_FINAL.pdf](https://img.scoop.co.nz/media/pdfs/2609/Te_Pti_Mori_Energy_Sovereignty_Policy_FINAL.pdf)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori has today its Energy Sovereignty policy, a plan to cut power costs, build Aotearoa’s energy future and shift ownership into the hands of whānau, hapū, iwi and communities.

“Every party is talking about generating more electricity. We’re asking the question they keep avoiding: who will own it?” said Te Pāti Co-Leader Rawiri Waititi

“If we replace fossil fuels with renewables but leave ownership and profits concentrated in the same hands, we haven’t transformed the system. We’ve just changed the technology.

“Participation is not sovereignty. Ownership is.”

Te Pāti Māori will:

• Establish a $1 billion Energy Sovereignty Fund to build Māori and community-owned energy assets.

• Develop a long-term National Energy Plan.

• Give regulators stronger powers to act against excessive pricing and profits.

• Establish fair value so whānau and communities are properly paid for the energy they generate and store.

• Set a pathway to Energy Sovereignty by 2035.

Co-Leader Debbie Ngarewa-Packer said the renewable transition cannot become the next extractive economy.

“Our whenua, wai and resources have generated wealth for others for generations. We will not allow that history to repeat itself under a green label.

“We want whānau generating power, marae storing it, iwi owning generation, Māori businesses building it and the wealth staying in our communities.

“Other parties want to build more power. We want our people to own it.

Cut the Power. Build the Power. Own the Power.

Power to the people.”

Note: Te Pati Moari Energy Sovereignty Policy

# Te Pāti Māori Launches Kai Sovereignty Policy

*Monday, 21 September 2026, 2:24 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2609/S00211/te-pati-maori-launches-kai-sovereignty-policy.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2609/S00211/te-pati-maori-launches-kai-sovereignty-policy.htm)

## Full text

Afford the kai. Grow the kai. Own the system.

Te Pāti Māori MP for Hauraki-Waikato Hana-Rāwhiti Maipi-Clarke unveiled Te Paati Māori Kai Sovereignty policy today from Kirikiriroa Social Supermarket run by Tamariki Tuu, Tamariki Ora.

A plan to help whānau afford kai now while rebuilding the power of communities to feed themselves.

“Aotearoa produces huge amounts of food, yet too many of our whānau are still struggling to put kai on the table,” said Maipi-Clarke.

“That is not a shortage of food. It is a failure of the system.”

The policy sets out a pathway from kai dependency to kai sovereignty by delivering immediate cost-of-living relief, investing in community and Māori food production, and building Māori ownership across the food system.

Te Pāti Māori will:

• introduce an Income Tax Kai Credit for people earning $60,000 or less, worth up to eight weeks of kai each year and estimated to support around 3 million people;

• establish a $100 million Community Kai Fund for home gardens, marae māra kai and community food farms;

• invest an additional $100 million into Mātai Ahuwhenua to grow regenerative Māori agriculture and diversified whenua-based production;

• invest $100 million into seed funding to support Māori-owned supermarket and retail alternatives;

• protect Māori seed, mātauranga and Indigenous plant whakapapa, including through WAI 262 protections.

“We do not want our people permanently dependent on food parcels, supermarket duopolies or corporate-controlled food chains.

“We want whānau growing kai, marae feeding communities, Māori producing kai, and our people owning more of the systems that distribute and sell it.

“Afford the kai. Grow the kai. Own the system.

“That is kai sovereignty.”

# Te Pāti Māori Launches Mana Takatāpui Policy

*Wednesday, 23 September 2026, 12:40 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2609/S00245/te-pati-maori-launches-mana-takatapui-policy.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2609/S00245/te-pati-maori-launches-mana-takatapui-policy.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori has today launched its Mana Takatāpui Policy, committing $200 million over three years and establishing an independent, Takatāpui governed Commission with real authority over Takatāpui specific funding.

Te Pāti Māori Co Leader Rawiri Waititi says the policy is built on a simple principle: Nothing about Takatāpui without Takatāpui.

“For too long, decisions have been made about Takatāpui without Takatāpui. Our policy changes who holds the power,” Waititi said.

“We are not creating another advisory group that Government can choose to listen to or ignore. We are establishing an independent Takatāpui governed Commission with authority and guaranteed, ring fenced funding.”

The policy commits $200 million over three years across healthcare, mental health, housing, safety, education and culture, while investing directly in Takatāpui led organisations.

It includes gender affirming kaupapa Māori healthcare, Takatāpui led mental health and suicide prevention, safe housing pathways, protection from violence and hate, stronger cultural connection, and safer education pathways.

“Takatāpui have always been part of us. They are our tamariki, our mokopuna, our aunties and uncles, our cousins, our kaumātua and our whānau.

“This is rangatiratanga in practice. Not simply asking our people what they need, but giving them the authority and resources to build it.

“Our message to our Takatāpui whānau is simple: you belong. You are Māori. You are whole. You carry whakapapa, tikanga and mana.”

Te Pāti Māori has today announced its Party List for the 2026 General Election, reaffirming its candidate-vote strategy by selecting just one list candidate outside its seven Māori electorate candidates.

Lance Norman, General Secretary of Te Pāti Māori, was selected unanimously as the Party’s additional list candidate.

“This list proves we are putting our money where our mouth is,” Te Pāti Māori Co-Leader Rawiri Waititi said.

documents/2026-10-06-te-pati-maori-backs.text:
# Te Pāti Māori Backs Kōhanga Reo And Kura With Long-Term Investment

*Tuesday, 6 October 2026, 7:49 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00052/te-pati-maori-backs-kohanga-reo-and-kura-with-long-term-investment.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00052/te-pati-maori-backs-kohanga-reo-and-kura-with-long-term-investment.htm)

## Full text

Te Pāti Māori will back the future of Māori-medium education with long-term investment in kōhanga reo and kura Māori, giving whānau certainty to build, grow and strengthen te reo Māori for future generations, Co-leader Rawiri Waititi and Hauraki-Waikato MP Hana-Rāwhiti Maipi-Clarke announced today in Rotorua.

“Kōhanga reo and kura Māori are the heartbeat of te reo Māori revitalisation. They need secure, long-term investment that reflects what they mean to our tamariki, our whānau and the future of Aotearoa.

“This is tino rangatiratanga in education. Māori-medium education must be able to plan, build and grow with certainty,” said Rawiri Waititi.

“From new kōhanga reo to upgraded kura, this is about giving whānau the support and certainty they need to raise tamariki in te reo Māori.

“Our tamariki deserve to learn in environments that are fit for purpose, with the buildings, kaiako and resources needed to support them to thrive,” said Hana-Rāwhiti Maipi-Clarke.

Te Pāti Māori will establish a Te Kōhanga Reo Act and lock in secure annual baseline funding for kōhanga reo.

It will invest $20 million a year in a dedicated capital fund, alongside a $50 million investment to address the backlog of around 80 kōhanga reo needing new builds or refurbishment.

The policy will fund 20 new kōhanga reo over three years, with priorities set alongside Te Kōhanga Reo National Trust to ensure investment reaches the communities that need it most.

For kura Māori, Te Pāti Māori will commit $1.25 billion over five years through a ring-fenced property investment plan. This includes $250 million a year to upgrade kura property and support the continued growth of Māori-medium education.

Te Pāti Māori will also restore Te Ahu o Te Reo Māori, with $30 million a year to strengthen te reo Māori capability across the education workforce.

documents/2026-10-12-te-pati-maori-annou.title: Te Pāti Māori Announces Toi Māori Authority And Artist Income Programme
documents/2026-10-12-te-pati-maori-annou.text:
# Te Pāti Māori Announces Toi Māori Authority And Artist Income Programme

*Monday, 12 October 2026, 3:17 pm Press Release: Te Pati Maori* — [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00101/te-pati-maori-announces-toi-maori-authority-and-artist-income-programme.htm](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00101/te-pati-maori-announces-toi-maori-authority-and-artist-income-programme.htm)

## Full text

Today in Ōtautahi, Te Pāti Māori has announced the establishment of an independent Toi Māori Authority and a continuing, two-year rotational income programme for Māori artists contributing to mātauranga Māori.

The authority will be independent of Creative New Zealand, resourced at parity with it, and governed by tohunga toi from across Māori art forms and iwi.

The income programme will support 1,000 artists at a time, providing paid work for 30 hours a week over two years. Places will then rotate to a new cohort of artists.

Co-Leader Rawiri Waititi said colonisation targeted Māori tohunga, artists, and storytellers because they carried the knowledge and identity of their people.

“Our identity is inseparable from our art forms. Successive governments have allowed the harm to Toi Māori to continue. This is about putting decisions in Māori hands and properly backing the artists who carry our mātauranga forward.

“When our creativity is strong, our people are strong.”

This investment will strengthen and protect the transmission of mātauranga Māori at home and internationally, it will support the oranga and livelihoods of our artists, and it will ensure that all mokopuna of Aotearoa grow up surrounded by mātauranga Māori in all of its forms.

# A Kiwi Tax Plan — Te Pāti Māori Policy Manifesto 2026: Tax

Source: [https://img.scoop.co.nz/media/pdfs/2608/A_Kiwi_Tax_Plan.pdf](https://img.scoop.co.nz/media/pdfs/2608/A_Kiwi_Tax_Plan.pdf). Attached by Te Pāti Māori to its 26 Aug 2026 press release (Scoop PA2608/S00238).

> Extraction notes: text is reproduced in the PDF's content-stream order, page by page. Only whitespace and glyph markup were normalised (bullet glyphs shown as •, decorative icons removed). Designed layouts mean page headers, side labels and table cells can appear out of visual order; consult the PDF for layout. No words were added, removed or reworded.

```text
A tax system that serves people, whenua,
and mokopuna.
For decades, the tax system in Aotearoa has
privileged wealth over work, property over
people, and extraction over care. Māori have

low wages, insecure housing, underfunded
```

### Page 1

```text
Kai Sovereignty
Te Pāti Māori Policy Manifesto 2026 • 2
Context
Agriculture is one of Aotearoa’s most significant primary industries, yet two of its key products; dairy and
meat, are almost exclusively export products. Around 95 percent of milk and more than 80 percent of meat
are exported overseas.
Leading companies in this industry are causing detrimental harm to our taiao as they continue to intensify
production at the expense of land, water and soil. At the same time, many people in Aotearoa cannot afford
to put basic kai on the table.
It is unacceptable that Aotearoa exploits the environment to provide food for the world while so many
whānau experience food poverty, compounded by rising costs and generations of entrenched poverty.
Our Position
We need sustainable ways to provide more food for everyone in Aotearoa while breaking the stranglehold
that monopolies have on food supply; across production, distribution and retail.
Our vision is to facilitate and support the transition of Māori from kai dependency to kai sovereignty: to feed
the community, teach the community to feed themselves, and empower them to feed each other.
We acknowledge Māori growers, hunters, regenerative agriculture farmers, related business owners,
governance leaders, and kaupapa Māori and Indigenous researchers who have kept tūpuna practices alive.
We must return to our traditional practices and customs of gathering kai because our sustenance can no
longer be in the hands of corporate-controlled food chains.
Our Vision
• Traditional practices, customs and ceremonies of gathering kai are revitalised.
• Whānau and communities have safe, clean and pure kai.
• Food security is realised and food poverty is eliminated.
• Soil is protected and restored.
• Independent and collaborative Māori-led approaches to kai are established.
Why community capability matters
Normalising the growing and distribution of kai at whānau and community level saves money, promotes
healthy lifestyles, and builds unity and purpose. It strengthens our collective tools and knowledge for the
benefit of all.
Marae have been at the forefront as first responders, distributing kai through national and civil emergency
events such as Covid-19, Cyclone Gabrielle and flooding. They must be supported to continue these
essential services.
```

```text
Kai Sovereignty
Te Pāti Māori Policy Manifesto 2026 • 3

1. Protect the whakapapa of kai
The kai we consume has whakapapa and sits within ecosystems that we are also part of. Seeds hold
whakapapa and must not be tampered with. Decisions about flora, fauna and the wider environment that
are symbiotic with Māori culture must be conceived of and determined by Tangata Whenua.
• Honour WAI 262 and reject research and commercialisation of Indigenous plant species undertaken

whānau, hapū, iwi and Māori organisations and partnering with the sectors and agencies that influence our
ability to feed ourselves.

and justice.
• Mandate the Board to lead work addressing hunger, poverty and inequality, and to ensure struggling

Kai sovereignty requires the growing and distribution of kai to become normal at whānau and community

• Establish Crown-funded kai sovereignty scholarships for rangatahi to pursue food sciences, marine
biology and primary-industry skills.
$100 million for whānau, marae and community food systems.
4. Build Māori production capability
Tangata Whenua must be supported to restore our capacity to feed our own people while growing our
economic base. We will reduce dependence on agribusiness and corporate-controlled food chains by

• Invest an additional $100 million into a Mātai Ahuwhenua agricultural innovation fund to support small-
scale and diversified pāmu/whenua blocks that prioritise regenerative and organic farming practices,

• Fund regenerative and organic farming training and technical programmes, including support for
agroforestry.
• Support garden-to-market food production that strengthens both food security and regional
development.
```

```text
Kai Sovereignty
Te Pāti Māori Policy Manifesto 2026 • 4
$100 million to support regenerative Māori agriculture and diversified whenua-based production.
5. Build Māori-owned retail alternatives
The supermarket duopoly has a stranglehold over food retail in Aotearoa. It must be broken so that Māori
and other independent grocers can gain a foothold in the market.
• Secure Crown or council-owned land in commercially viable areas

From kai dependency to kai sovereignty.
Te Pāti Māori will ensure communities are fed, communities are taught to feed themselves and empower
```

```text
Entrench the Māori electorates
```

```text
Since 1840, the retention and return of land has been the most significant
political aspiration of Tangata Whenua, the unifying struggle of the tino

Ngāwha and Te Kuri a Pāoa in the early 2000s.
Over the last decade, the Land Back movement has stretched across the
Indigenous world and breathed new life into the fight for land and sovereignty.
In Aotearoa, this was demonstrated by the successful four-year Ihumātao land
occupation.

empowered to hear historical grievances dating back to 1840.
The strong desire of the Crown and tangata whenua to settle historical Treaty

But as Moana Jackson has so often said, treaties are not settled, they’re
honoured.
Te Tiriti is a document that is the foundation of a living, evolving relationship
between tangata whenua and the Crown. Both parties to Te Tiriti must
continually strive to meet the obligations it sets out and implement the three
articles in everything we do.
```

```text
the introduction of constitutional guarantees of the tino Rangatiratanga and
```

```text
consistent with who we are as a nation. 70,000 people signed Te Pāti Māori’s
```

```text
Mana Motuhake Policy
Ka whawhai tonu mātou, ake, ake, ake!
Te Pāti Māori will end the fiscal envelope and insert relativity clauses into all Te
Tiriti settlements, to ensure there is parity with Ngāi Tahu and Waikato-Tainui.
We would also empower the Waitangi Tribunal by legislating to make their
recommendations binding on the Crown, and we would work to implement all
WAI claim recommendations that have been unaddressed over the last several
decades.
1. Ending full and final settlements and large natural groupings
The Crown’s “full and final” policy - wanting to settle all the historical claims with
an iwi grouping at once in one settlement, is a breach of Te Tiriti.
Te Pāti Māori wants to see an end to “full and final” settlements, to allow
historical claims to be revisited, and new claims brought, where situations have
changed or whānau, hapū or iwi groups were shut out of the original
negotiations.
Often groups are shut out of negotiations due the Crown’s large natural
groupings policy, which doesn’t recognise the mandate of whānau, hapū and
relatively small iwi. Time and time again hapū with legitimate claims have been
shut down in negotiations and this has caused further harm. This divide and rule
tactic has created new Te Tiriti breaches even as the Crown tries to settle
historical breaches.
Hapū are the primary political unit in te ao Māori. Te Pāti Māori uphold
hapūtanga and recognise that it was the rangatira of hapū that signed Te Tiriti,
and so we would ensure that the Crown negotiates with whānau and hapū and
recognises their mana whenua.
Ensuring effective Crown oversight
1. Electoral reform
It’s critical that our people are able to participate in Crown decision-making
processes fairly and accessibly. The threat of removing Māori representation is
often used as a weapon against our people. We must entrench the Māori
electorates and require all local and regional councils to have both Māori wards
and mana whenua representation.
2. Parliamentary Commissioner for Te Tiriti o Waitangi
```

### Page 8

```text
Mana Motuhake Policy
Ka whawhai tonu mātou, ake, ake, ake!
Te Pāti Māori will establish a Parliamentary Commissioner for Te Tiriti o Waitangi
to provide oversight and ensure that the Crown meets its obligations under the
Treaty partnership.
Currently there is no oversight of legislation or Crown departments and agencies
from a Te Tiriti perspective. That’s unacceptable. The Crown has an
environmental commission, a human rights commission, a disability commission
– it’s well past time to establish a Treaty commission.
The Parliamentary Commissioner for Te Tiriti o Waitangi will have functions and
powers to enable them to:
Review and investigate priority issues of concern
Provide advice to Parliament
Contribute to public debate through the provision of information and
analysis
The Commissioner will be appointed for a five-year term on the
recommendation of hapū, iwi and Māori organisations. Based on the budgets
for other parliamentary commissioners, establishing this office would require
approximately $4m in funding per annum.
3. Te Tiriti o Waitangi impact statements
Currently, Te Tiriti is only formally considered in legislation and regulation when
the Government considers it relevant. However, we know that all Crown laws
and regulations have impacts on tangata whenua and on the implementation of
Te Tiriti.
Te Pāti Māori will ensure that all pieces of legislation, executive regulations and
cabinet papers are required to have Te Tiriti impact statements
```

```text
ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY POLICY 2026 | POLICY
TE PĀTI MĀORI • ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY • 1
Energy Sovereignty Policy
Executive Summary
Energy is power.
It powers our homes, our businesses, our marae, our transport and our economy. However, too
many of our people remain customers of an energy system they do not own and have little
control over.
We pay the bills. Our whenua, wai and natural resources support the system. Our communities
host the infrastructure; yet ownership, control and profit remain concentrated elsewhere.
Te Pāti Māori will change that.
Our Energy Sovereignty policy is a just transition pathway to transform who produces, owns
and benefits from energy in Aotearoa.
CUT THE POWER
Lower energy
costs for whānau
and reduce our
dependence on
fossil fuels.
BUILD THE POWER
Invest in renewable generation, storage,
infrastructure, Māori businesses, skills,
system planning and community
resilience. Connection rules and costs
must not lock smaller Māori and
community projects out of the system.
OWN THE POWER
Shift capital,
ownership and control
into the hands of
whānau, hapū, iwi and
communities.
Te Pāti Māori will establish a just transition pathway towards Energy Sovereignty by
2035.
This is not about subsidising energy consumption, it is about building assets, shifting capital
and shifting ownership. It is about moving our people from being customers of the energy
system to becoming producers, builders, investors and owners.
```

### Page 2

```text
ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY POLICY 2026 | POLICY
TE PĀTI MĀORI • ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY • 2
Context
Aotearoa is entering a major energy transformation. Homes, transport, businesses and industry
will increasingly move away from fossil fuels and towards electricity and other renewable
energy sources.
That transition will require significant investment in generation, storage, transmission,
distribution networks, infrastructure and workforce capability. It also presents one of the largest
economic opportunities of the next generation.
Greater electrification and renewable generation mean we can produce more of the energy we
need here at home, reduce our dependence on imported fossil fuels and keep more of our
energy spending circulating within Aotearoa.
But Te Pāti Māori will not support a transition that simply replaces one form of extraction with
another. We will not accept renewable infrastructure being built on or around Māori whenua
while Māori remain customers and somebody else owns the assets.
Our renewable energy future will draw on the full range of appropriate renewable resources,
including solar, wind, geothermal, hydro, bioenergy and emerging technologies, with
development subject to Te Tiriti, mana whenua authority and strong protections for the taiao.
Anchored in Te Tiriti
Energy Sovereignty is anchored in Te Tiriti o Waitangi.
There is no climate justice without Tiriti justice.
The transition to renewable energy must uphold tino rangatiratanga and must not reproduce an
economic model where value is extracted from Māori communities while ownership, decision-
making and economic benefit accumulate elsewhere.
Māori must have meaningful rights and interests in ownership, governance, investment,
development, employment, procurement, benefit sharing and decisions affecting whenua, wai
and other taonga.
The renewable transition cannot become the next extractive economy. Renewable development
must honour Te Tiriti, protect mana whenua decision-making, uphold strong environmental
standards and avoid shifting environmental harm onto mokopuna generations.
Energy transformation must strengthen both tino rangatiratanga and intergenerational Māori
wealth.
```

### Page 3

```text
ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY POLICY 2026 | POLICY
TE PĀTI MĀORI • ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY • 3
1. Cut the Power: Lower Whānau Energy Costs
Te Pāti Māori will help whānau reduce their energy costs by making it easier to produce, store
and use more of their own energy.
We will support access to:
• Solar and batteries
• Energy-efficient appliances, heating and hot water
• Home electrification and EV charging
• Long-term, low-cost and zer o-interest finance
• Rates Assistance Scheme
Renters and whānau living in social housing must also benefit from the energy transition. We
will support renter-friendly energy solutions, community batteries and stronger electrification
standards across rental and social housing.
Crown-funded housing will be expected to lead the transition, with renewable energy and
electrification increasingly built into new developments.
Te Pāti Māori will establish a government backed loan scheme to provide long-term, low-cost
finance for homeowners, Māori landowners, papakāinga, marae and community energy
projects. This will support the installation of solar, batteries, efficient heating, hot water systems,
insulation, EV charging and other upgrades that permanently cut power costs. This financing
mechanism will be delivered through an expanded Ratepayer Assistance Scheme
This is not about permanently subsidising electricity bills. It is about investing in assets that
permanently reduce them.
THE PRINCIPLE
Invest in assets that permanently reduce power bills.
This is not about permanently subsidising electricity bills. It is about building household and
community energy capability.
2. Build the Power
Te Pāti Māori will invest in the infrastructure, capability and planning required to build the
energy system Aotearoa needs.
This means building more renewable generation, strengthening transmission and distribution
networks, investing in storage, growing the Māori energy workforce and ensuring local energy
systems are planned alongside national infrastructure.
```

### Page 4

```text
ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY POLICY 2026 | POLICY
TE PĀTI MĀORI • ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY • 4
Establish a $1 Billion Energy Sovereignty Fund
ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY FUND
$1 BILLION
Capital to build Māori and community ownership of productive energy assets.
Te Pāti Māori will establish a $1 billion Energy Sovereignty Fund to build Māori and community
ownership of the energy system.
We will reinvest at the scale of the wealth currently being extracted from our homes and
communities through the electricity system, and use that capital to build productive energy
assets owned by our people.
The Fund will invest in:
• Reducing household energy costs
• Marae and papakāinga energy resilience
• Māori-owned renewable generation
• Community batteries and microgrids
• Energy infrastructure on whenua Māori
• Māori energy businesses
• Skills, apprenticeships and workforce development
• Pathways for whānau, iwi and Māori entities to own productive energy assets
Establish a National Independence Energy Plan
We will establish a National Energy Independence Plan run by a National Energy
Independence Taskforce made up of iwi, sector groups and workforce operators.
Any situation where the private market is not setting the price of power, the market is being
regulated.
A fairness framework will be mandated to regulate pricing.
Te Pāti Māori will establish a whole-of-system National Energy Plan covering generation,
storage, transmission, distribution networks, household electrification, transport, industrial
demand, resilience, workforce development and Māori and community ownership.
The Plan will identify the renewable mix Aotearoa needs, including solar, wind, geothermal,
hydro, bioenergy and emerging technologies, and ensure national infrastructure and local
energy systems are planned together.
It will identify and fund the transmission and distribution upgrades required for new renewable
generation, community energy, electrification and storage.
```

### Page 5

```text
ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY POLICY 2026 | POLICY
TE PĀTI MĀORI • ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY • 5
Build the Power
Build a Māori Energy Workforce and Industry
Te Pāti Māori will create explicit pathways for Māori businesses, workers and training providers
across construction, electrical trades, solar and battery installation, engineering, maintenance,
energy services, transport electrification and emerging technologies.
Crown-funded energy investment will actively support Māori procurement, apprenticeships and
workforce development. The transition should create businesses, careers and intergenerational
capability owned by our people.
Build Rural Energy Capability
Te Pāti Māori will support farms and rural communities to become energy producers through
on-farm generation, energy storage, rural charging and distributed energy. Rural communities
should be owners and beneficiaries of the transition, not simply consumers facing new costs.
Build the infrastructure. Build the businesses. Build the workforce. Build the
capability.
3. Own the Power: Increase Māori and Community Ownership
Participation is not sovereignty. Ownership is.
Te Pāti Māori will deliberately increase Māori and community ownership of renewable energy
infrastructure.
The Energy Sovereignty Fund will use grants, concessional finance, guarantees, equity
investment and co-investment to enable whānau, hapū, iwi, marae, Māori landowners and
communities to acquire permanent ownership stakes in productive energy assets.
Ownership pathways will include whānau ownership, hapū and iwi equity, community and co-
operative ownership, Māori-Crown co-investment, joint ventures, Māori landowner investment
and Māori-owned business investment.
Crown investment will be designed to build Māori equity, not permanent Crown ownership.
We will create stronger pathways for mana whenua to participate as owners in major renewable
developments within their rohe and ensure Crown investment supports Māori equity rather than
simply consultation.
```

```text
ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY POLICY 2026 | POLICY
TE PĀTI MĀORI • ENERGY SOVEREIGNTY • 6
Fair Value for Whānau and Communities
Te Pāti Māori will establish a fair-value framework for distributed generation, battery storage
and grid services so households and communities are properly paid for energy and services
supplied back to the system.
This will support household solar, battery storage, community energy, microgrids, local energy
sharing and Māori-owned distributed generation.
If our people generate the power, store the power or strengthen the grid, they should be paid
fairly for it.
Regulate the Energy System in the Public Interest
Energy is essential national infrastructure. It must serve people before profit.
Te Pāti Māori will strengthen the powers of the Commerce Commission and Electricity Authority
to investigate excessive pricing and profits, strengthen competition and protect consumers.
We will ensure regulators have the power to intervene more structurally if regulation does not
deliver fair prices, genuine competition, consumer protection and fair access for Māori and
community-owned generation.
Regulatory tools will include pricing, market investigations and enforceable remedies.
We will remove unnecessary barriers that prevent whānau, Māori and communities from
generating, sharing, selling and trading energy.
Reduce Fossil-Fuel Dependence and Protect Our Sovereignty
Te Pāti Māori will support businesses, farms, transport and industry to move away from fossil
fuels where renewable energy and electrification are technically and economically viable.
The more energy we produce here at home, the less dependent we are on fossil fuels imported
from overseas. That means greater national resilience and economic sovereignty.
The renewable transition cannot become the next extractive economy.
Te Pāti Māori will also protect Māori energy data sovereignty. Information generated through
smart meters, community energy systems, storage, trading platforms and emerging
technologies must not become another resource extracted from our people without authority or
benefit.
Energy Sovereignty by 2035
Our 2035 goal is a just transition that delivers a measurable shift in affordability, capability,
ownership and control.
• By 2035 Te Pāti Māori will deliver measurable reductions in household energy costs and
measurable increases in Māori and community ownership of new renewable energy assets.
```
